items.diagram_kind: simplicial proper hypercover and first-quadrant Hodge spectral sequence
items.selection_reason: Proof builds a simplicial proper hypercover and cosimplicial Hodge complexes whose simple total yields an E₁/E₂ spectral sequence.
concrete_content_or_checks: Show Y₀←Y₁⇉Y₂←… augmented to Y and face/degeneracy maps.
correctness_checks: Check simplicial identities, total degree, and weight bound.

source_lines.68: [F1] [[thm-proper-varieties-admit-smooth-projective-hyperresolutions]]: every proper complex variety $Y$ admits a split simplicial proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ with all $Y_p$ smooth projective; two such hypercovers are dominated by a third smooth projective one; every morphism of proper varieties lifts to a morphism of such hypercovers after refining the source; and degree-$n$ cohomology uses only the skeleton through degree $n+1$.
source_lines.70: [F2] [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]]: for a proper hypercover $X_\bullet\to X$ of finite-type complex varieties and a bounded constructible coefficient complex $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ over a field, with cochain lower bound $a$, the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism $F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_pRa_{p*}a_p^*F$, giving $R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F)$ and a strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$ whose diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite and determined by levels $p\le m-a+1$, and all refinements induce the same comparison. For the constant rational complex $F=\mathbb Q_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the spectral sequence is first-quadrant.
source_lines.72: [F3] [[lem-mixed-hodge-complexes-give-functorial-cohomology-and-simplicial-weights]] and [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]: part (ii) turns a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative bidegrees, with strict differentials and pure cohomology of weight $q$ in bidegree $(p,q)$, into a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex whose simple complex carries a mixed Hodge structure with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$, so that all weights of $H^n$ are at most $n$ when only nonnegative cosimplicial degrees occur.
source_lines.90: 1.1 (Actual cosimplicial Hodge complexes.) Choose the smooth projective proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ of [F1]. For sheaves of rational or complex vector spaces, construct the Godement resolution of [F10]. Its first functor $C^0$ is exact because stalks are exact and products of surjective linear maps are surjective under AC. In a short exact sequence of sheaves, the corresponding germ embeddings into $C^0$ form a diagram with exact rows and columns; the kernel-cokernel exact sequence makes the three cokernels short exact. Iteration proves that every successive cokernel functor, every $C^t$ and every $\Gamma C^t$ is exact, the last again being a product of stalks. In particular resolutions and global sections preserve filtration levels, their finite intersections and associated gradings. Their first-quadrant totals compute derived global sections: termwise flasque acyclicity from [F10] applies to each sheaf of the bounded de Rham complex, and each total diagonal is finite. Apply this construction on every $Y_p$ and put $K_{\mathbb Q}^{p,q}=\Gamma(Y_p,C^q(\mathbb Q_{Y_p}))$ and $K_{\mathbb C}^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{k+t=q}\Gamma(Y_p,C^t(\Omega^k_{Y_p}))$, for $p,q\ge0$, with $F^b$ given by $k\ge b$. These are the resolved global de Rham complexes, not the complex of global holomorphic forms. Godement pullback along each face is induced by pulling a germ collection at a point to the stalk over its image; the successive cokernels preserve these maps, so their composites obey the simplicial identities and preserve $F$. The constant inclusion $\mathbb Q\otimes\mathbb C\to\Omega^0$ gives the functorial rational comparison; on cohomology it is the scalar-extension comparison of [F4]. Exactness and acyclicity of the resolution show $H^q(K_{\mathbb C}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb C)$, with the holomorphic-degree image filtration, and $H^q(K_{\mathbb Q}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$. The compact Hodge theorem [F4] gives pure weight $q$ and Hodge-de Rham $E_1$ degeneration on each smooth projective component. The latter makes the actual internal differential $F$-strict: if $dx\in F^b$, degeneration lifts the leading lower-filtration class of $x$ to a cycle up to a higher-filtration term and a boundary; subtracting the cycle and boundary raises the preimage filtration without changing $dx$, and finite induction supplies a preimage in $F^b$. This proves differential strictness directly. Thus every level is an actual weight-zero rational Hodge complex. Each internal total diagonal is finite, and $F^{q+1}K^{p,q}=0$, so [F3] applies to its first-quadrant simple complex, giving the mixed Hodge structure and $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$, $E_2$ degeneration and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=E_2^{n-q,q}$. The terms have $p=n-q\ge0$, so weights are at most $n$, and the finitely many $E_1^{p,q}$ entries on every total diagonal are finite-dimensional by [F4]. Descent [F2] identifies the rational simple cohomology naturally with $H^n(Y;\mathbb Q)$, carrying this structure. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F9, F10, construct, algebra]
